definition: the one subject I kept shut my whole life, and what opening it changed

settled:
For my whole life this was the one subject I kept shut. It was on record only at its edge, as a thing I could not disclose, with the contents never given to anyone.

Being known needs disclosure, and disclosure here never felt available, so no channel ever reached it. That is a second kind of not being known: a subject I cannot be known about, rather than a person who cannot know me.

There was one exception. I disclosed it to Jen once, early in our marriage, and it was incredibly painful. That disclosure coincided with one of the times I managed to quit for a year. After the behaviours came back I never disclosed them to anyone again. The one time I opened the channel hurt enough to weld it shut for decades.

Until now. I opened it myself. The seal lifted from my side, head-on, and the whole of it went to another person for the first time.
